ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In order to study the structure and function of proteins, it is often necessary to separate and purify proteins from biological materials. A student used gel chromatography to separate and purify 3 kinds of proteins, A, B, and C, from a certain biological material, and performed SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis on the 3 purified proteins. The results are shown in the figure ("+" and "-" respectively represent the anode and cathode of the electrophoresis tank). It is known that the relative molecular mass of A is twice that of B, and both A and B are composed of one peptide chain. Answer the question: Gel chromatography can separate proteins according to differences in the relative molecular mass of proteins. Judging from the figure, among the 3 proteins A, B, and C, which protein is eluted last from the gel chromatography column?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the results of SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. The three lanes above are labeled A, B, and C respectively; the upper right end is labeled "-", and the lower end is labeled "+", indicating that the protein bands migrate downward toward the anode direction. The A lane has one band, located relatively high; the B lane has one band, located lower than A and closer to "+"; the C lane has two bands, one near the top and one near the bottom. Then reason: In SDS-PAGE, after proteins are denatured, they are mainly separated according to the relative molecular mass of peptide chains. The smaller the molecular mass, the farther they migrate, and the closer they are to the anode. A and B are both composed of one peptide chain, and the stem states that the relative molecular mass of A is twice that of B. The figure also shows that B migrates farther, so B is smaller than A. C shows two bands, indicating that C is composed of multiple peptide chains, and the relative molecular mass of its complete protein should be the sum of the relative molecular masses of the peptide chains, so overall it will not be smaller than B. In gel chromatography, proteins with larger relative molecular mass are eluted first, and proteins with smaller relative molecular mass are eluted later, so the one last eluted from the gel chromatography column is B, which has the smallest relative molecular mass.
